newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine beer industry shows signs of recovery.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine beer industry shows signs of recovery.

text.p: Ukraine's beer industry is half the size it was before independence five years ago, but brewers are trying to get it back on tap, industry officials said at the first national beer show.

"I would say that five years ago the industry produced 30 litres per person. Now it's 15 litres per person," said Arkady Okolot, deputy chief executive of former beer monopoly AT Ukrpyvo, which operates 65 breweries and is a show co-sponsor.
The brewing industry was in a poor state at independence in 1991, inheriting ancient equipment, an inefficient labour force, primitive distribution systems and no money for improvements.
Survival was the name of the game then, Okolot said, but now the industry is showing signs of recovery.
"There are at least 100 breweries in Ukraine. In recent times I would say at least 50 new microbreweries have started operating," he said.
Over 40 breweries, filtration system companies and label manufacturers were taking part in the show, he said, adding, "We did not have room for everyone wanting to participate."
A main task for brewers is creating an appeal for beer amongst Ukraine's population of 51 million. Whisky (horilka) and cheap red wine dominate the market for alcoholic beverages.

Okolot said horilka holds the price advantage, with a 1.5 litre bottle sold for 2.5 hryvnya ($1.50) and a half-litre bottle of local light or dark beer, made from locally-produced hops, selling for about about 70 cents.
Many Ukrainians are also suffering from a post-Soviet beer hangover, when the only type of beer brewed was often cloudy and had unidentifiable things floating around in it.
Okolot said the average Ukrainian's experience of beer-drinking was to buy it from a barrel on the street and drink it from the first available container, like a dirty jar.
"Here a person cannot rest and have a beer at a cafe and restaurant," he said. "We have to develop a culture so the lifestyle creates the possibility for a person to sit down and have a beer."
